content.title: About
content.content: Safflower oil is extracted from the seeds of the safflower plant (Carthamus tinctorius). It is light‑yellow, has a mild nutty aroma, and is rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, especially linoleic acid (omega‑6). It is widely used in cooking, cosmetics, and the food industry.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Safflower is cultivated in dry regions, notably Russia, India, and the United States.
The seeds contain up to 80 % linoleic acid, making the oil one of the richest sources of this fatty acid.
In the early 20th century, safflower oil was used as a cheaper alternative to more expensive vegetable oils.
Because of its bright yellow hue, safflower oil is sometimes called “sun oil.”
In cosmetics, it is valued for its ability to improve the skin’s barrier function.

items.title: Rich in polyunsaturated fats
items.content: Linoleic acid helps maintain normal blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: The oil moisturizes the epidermis, speeds up healing of minor wounds, and reduces inflammation.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory potential
items.content: Omega‑6 fatty acids can help reduce inflammatory processes when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Antioxidants and fatty acids contribute to normal immune function.

items.title: High omega‑6 content
items.content: Excessive intake without adequate omega‑3 balance may promote inflammation.

items.title: Allergy risk
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to safflower oil.

items.title: Not suitable for high‑heat frying
items.content: When overheated, the oil can oxidize and form harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Safflower oil is used in salad dressings, marinades, light sautéing, and baking. In cosmetics it is added to creams, lotions, and facial or hair masks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the oil in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated to prevent oxidation. Typical shelf life is 12‑18 months.
